title: Force, Mass, and Acceleration in One Dimension
learningObjectives: Explain that an object maintains constant velocity when net force is zero.
Use net force and mass to calculate acceleration in one dimension.
Predict that acceleration decreases as mass increases for a fixed net force.

sources.title: Newton's Laws of Motion — NASA Glenn Research Center, Beginner's Guide to Aeronautics

evidence.quote: If there is no net force acting on the object, then the object will maintain a constant velocity.
This tendency to resist changes in a state of motion is inertia.

explanations.text: When net force is zero, velocity stays constant because objects resist changes in motion.

evidence.quote: The acceleration of an object depends on the mass of the object and the amount of force applied.

explanations.text: Acceleration is determined by net force and mass, so a larger applied force produces larger acceleration for the same mass.

evidence.quote: The amount of acceleration is also inversely proportional to the mass of the object

explanations.text: For the same net force, a heavier object accelerates less than a lighter object.

behavioralTests.name: zero net force produces zero acceleration

predictions.prompt: A 4 kg model aircraft experiences 12 N net forward force. What is its acceleration?
A 5 kg model aircraft experiences -15 N net force. What is its acceleration?
